findings: The public function-action helper composes the existing shared-script snapshot and lazy actor scope, retaining overlay order/duplicate indices and tracked-row order. It reads broadcasts and sounds, restores note-field column/spline state, measures side effects, resets/rewinds all touched actors, restores output globals and clocks, then rewinds outer script state in native order. First callback return, inputs, replaced globals and saved note identities stay rooted.

Column snapshots retain original player/note-field/column/handler/spline identities plus independently cloned native fields. Original point-table aliases can remain mutated while the restored spline receives its cloned pre-probe points. Named-child lookup uses the existing raw fast path or full native merge. Cleanup has no Store lock held across Lua/reentry/GC.

The action scope adds before/after actor-restoration stages to the existing touched-function driver. The ordinary touched helper keeps its previous path. Cleanup callbacks are still allocated before activation, touched identities freeze before command-local rewind, and fresh VM entries allow cleanup after fatal instruction aborts.

Focused v1 caught a Rust borrow error in stack-backed text conversion. Copied bytes out of that borrow; focused v2 then passed four cases and failed only because the new fixture used nonexistent SOUNDMAN in both engines. Corrected it to the existing SOUND name without changing its capture assertions.

Focused v3 passed four cases and exposed that the Rust adapter had never installed the existing SOUND global. This is an inventoried production gap, not a request for additional StepMania behavior. The native SOUND methods and resource/call/runtime-event recording were ported into the song adapter.

SOUND retains DimMusic, StopMusic, PlayMusicPart, PlayOnce, PlayAnnouncer, GetPlayerBalance and IsTimingDelayed. Side effects, original returned manager identity, method-argument offset, string-only path input, native path lookup/no trimming, audio filtering, deduplication, repeated call capture, partial errors and runtime queued-startup/message provenance are preserved.

Focused v4 passed all seven cases, including two added SOUND comparisons. Static review then used the existing HostCall string coercion directly instead of allocating a callback/channel per output entry, tightened SOUND raw-path input to the actual native read_string type rule, and added a restoration-callback error/partial-state case.

The first-return lifetime test now keeps its weak table on an actor, outside outer script-table rewind, so clearing snapshot entries cannot mask a leaked return root. It checks retention during column restoration GC, collection of extra returns, final root release, and side-effect counting after output collection but before actor rewind.

Focused v5 passed all eight cases. Column restoration errors retain native actor/global/clock partial state, release the private scope, and allow later probes. Final unchanged-source regression run passed 350 tests across 24 targets. All 1,221 watched inputs match both checks; formatting passes; the exact earlier 109-case activation prefix remains intact. Clippy output is bitwise identical to its established 166-warning/cmd.rs:349-error baseline. Stable/deferred message/easing/tree/wrapper/global-reference/proxy/derived-output compilation, production live/session/navigation/fallback/cache/unconditional cutover and the original application/content/final-source/link/performance gates remain required. Production songs still use legacy; interpreter/C API removal milestones remain closed.
